reports.title: Rocket Lab Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results: Posts Record Revenue, $1.2 Billion or 52% Sequential Quarterly Backlog Growth, Positive GAAP Operating Cash Flow, and Guides to Record Revenue and Gross Margin Expansion in Q4 2026

guidance.heading: Fourth Quarter 2026 Guidance
section: For the fourth quarter of 2026, Rocket Lab expects:
•GAAP Operating Expenses between $162 million and $168 million.
•Non-GAAP Operating Expenses between $136 million and $142 million.
•Adjusted EBITDA loss of between $14 million and $20 million.
•Basic Weighted Average Common Shares Outstanding of 681 million, including approximately 41 million of Series A Convertible Participating Preferred Shares.

desk.headline: Record revenue up 73% to $268m, beat; wider loss per share; Q4 revenue guided to $270–290m
results: Revenue jumped 73% to a record $268m, ahead of the $257m analysts expected; product sales nearly doubled.
The loss per share widened to $0.12 from $0.03, hit by a $27m debt-repayment charge, $21m of deal costs and a tax charge instead of last year's tax benefit.
Backlog rose 52% in three months to about $3.6bn, helped by roughly $1bn of new launch contracts and $470m for space systems.
Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $18m from $26m, but non-GAAP gross margin slipped to 38.4% from 41.9%.
Operating cash flow turned positive at $7.2m; share sales lifted cash to $4.4bn, which funds the pending Iridium purchase.

guidance.summary: Rocket Lab only guides one quarter ahead. For Q4 it expects another record revenue quarter and a higher gross margin, with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $14–20m.

points: Neutron's first launch has slipped to 2027 after a fault in a propellant-tank part; a replacement has been built but no date was set.
Some Neutron missions were booked at a higher $70m base price; management chose price over volume as launch capacity tightens.
Sixteen Neutron launches are already booked; eight new Neutron missions worth about $515m were signed in the quarter.
The Iridium deal is fully funded and approved by Iridium shareholders, but still awaits regulators.
Cash flow will stay lumpy: big satellite milestone payments helped Q3, and Neutron spending keeps free cash flow negative.
call.source: Call coverage: MarketBeat via Yahoo Finance, 9 Nov 2026

watch: A firm date for Neutron's first flight in 2027.
Regulatory approval and closing of the Iridium acquisition.
Whether Q4 delivers the guided gross-margin recovery to 39–41% (non-GAAP).
